claims.text: Most medium and large SaaS companies will struggle, spectacularly, in the medium term, as companies and individuals build what they want instead of renting an approximation.
claims.quote: Most medium and large SaaS companies will struggle, spectacularly, in the medium term

claims.text: Nokia met the arrival of the mobile phone by becoming the mobile phone company and dominated the category for fifteen years.
claims.quote: Nokia met the arrival of the mobile phone by becoming the mobile phone company, and dominated the category for fifteen years.

claims.text: Nokia met the arrival of the iPhone with fifteen years of success to protect and was gone from the category within seven.
claims.quote: Nokia met the arrival of the iPhone and was gone from the category within seven.

claims.text: AI is not the deciding factor because AI is available to both sides; the incumbents have the same models plus more data, engineers and money, and have not won.
claims.quote: AI is not the deciding factor, because AI is available to both sides.

claims.text: In the first week of February 2026, after Anthropic shipped plug-ins for its Claude Cowork agent, software stocks fell off a cliff.
claims.quote: after Anthropic shipped plug-ins for its Claude Cowork agent covering legal, sales, marketing and data analysis, software stocks fell off a cliff.

claims.text: An equity trader at Jefferies, Jeffrey Favuzza, named it the SaaSpocalypse.
claims.quote: An equity trader at Jefferies, Jeffrey Favuzza, gave it a name: the SaaSpocalypse.

claims.text: Roughly $285 billion left the software sector in about 48 hours.
claims.quote: Roughly $285 billion left the sector in about 48 hours.

value.unit: billion USD lost in about 48 hours

claims.text: The S&P 500 software and services index dropped 13% over five sessions and sat 26% below its October peak.
claims.quote: the S&P 500 software and services index dropped 13% over five sessions and sat 26% below its October peak

claims.text: Forrester published a piece titled, without hedging, SaaS as we know it is dead.
claims.quote: Forrester published a piece titled, without hedging, SaaS as we know it is dead.

claims.text: By July the software ETF was down 10.5% for the year against an S&P 500 up 10.8%, and by September it had rallied about 40% from its April low.
claims.quote: By July the software ETF was down 10.5% for the year against an S&P 500 up 10.8%

value.unit: percent down for the year, software ETF

claims.text: The recovery argument is that the database is the moat, not the interface or the seat; that is not a rebuttal of the apocalypse, it is the apocalypse, priced.
claims.quote: That is not a rebuttal of the apocalypse. It is the apocalypse, priced.

claims.text: J.P. Morgan's Mark Murphy called it an illogical leap to expect every company to write and maintain a bespoke product to replace every layer, and the owner agrees they will not maintain it.
claims.quote: an illogical leap to extrapolate Claude Cowork Plugins to an expectation that every company will write and maintain a bespoke product to replace every layer.

claims.text: Freshworks surveyed 8,698 people in 2022 and found 91% frustrated by inadequate workplace technology.
claims.quote: found 91% frustrated by inadequate workplace technology

value.unit: percent of people surveyed frustrated by workplace technology

claims.text: Pendo analysed 615 instrumented products and found 80% of features in the average software product are rarely or never used.
claims.quote: 80% of features in the average software product are rarely or never used

value.unit: percent of features rarely or never used, across 615 products

claims.text: Standish's famous 64% came from a 2002 keynote based on four internal applications and should never have been generalised, as Mike Cohn documents.
claims.quote: it came from a 2002 keynote based on four internal applications, and should never have been generalised.

claims.text: Zylo's 2025 SaaS Management Index puts the average organisation's waste on unused licences at $21 million a year, up 14.2% on the year before.
claims.quote: $21 million a year, up 14.2% on the year before

value.unit: million USD a year wasted on unused licences per average organisation

claims.text: SaaS spend is $4,830 per employee, a large enterprise runs around 660 applications, and lines of business control 70% of that spend.
claims.quote: SaaS spend is $4,830 per employee. A large enterprise runs around 660 applications.

value.unit: applications run by a large enterprise

claims.text: A Deloitte survey found 73% of companies used Excel to prepare VAT returns, and 78% of British companies say spreadsheets support key financial decisions.
claims.quote: A Deloitte survey found 73% of companies used Excel to prepare VAT returns

value.unit: percent of companies using Excel for VAT returns

claims.text: The persistence of Excel is not a failure of users to adopt; it is the clearest evidence that SaaS failed them, because Excel is the tool where they control the shape.
claims.quote: The persistence of Excel is not a failure of users to adopt. It is the clearest evidence we have that SaaS failed them

claims.text: The mechanism underneath is the climatic pattern Simon Wardley names: past success breeds inertia.
claims.quote: the mechanism underneath is the one Simon Wardley names as a climatic pattern: past success breeds inertia.

claims.text: In Wardley's words, the pre-existing installed base causes inertia to the change, and users fixated on a legacy world have a bias towards it.
claims.quote: The pre-existing installed base causes inertia to the change.

claims.text: Above a certain size a company's decisions turn to locking the customer in: it does not make it easy to leave, to get data or schema out, or to use a first-class API.
claims.quote: The easiest way to see it is to look at what they do not build.

claims.text: On the map, the SaaS product has slid right: what was custom became a product, and the product is commoditising into a substrate, a database, a message bus, a state machine.
claims.quote: The SaaS product has slid right. What was custom-built became a product, and what was a product is now commoditising into a substrate

claims.text: Vibe coding is Andrej Karpathy's term from February 2025, and by November it was Collins Dictionary's word of the year.
claims.quote: The term is Andrej Karpathy's, from February 2025, and by November it was Collins Dictionary's word of the year.

claims.text: What vibe coding actually describes is people writing very good briefs, which product owners always did in an environment with a catastrophically slow loop.
claims.quote: let me say what it actually describes: people writing very good briefs.

claims.text: Show me a SaaS company and the owner will show you a company that is highly inefficient at developing software, because few invested in non-functional requirements.
claims.quote: show me a SaaS company and I will show you a company that is highly inefficient at developing software.

claims.text: Stripe found engineers spend 17.3 hours a week, 42% of their working time, on maintenance and bad code, costed at $85 billion a year.
claims.quote: 17.3 hours a week, 42% of their working time, on maintenance and bad code

value.unit: hours a week on maintenance and bad code

claims.text: In the 2024 DORA report only 19% of teams are elite performers, the high cluster shrank from 31% to 22%, and elite teams deploy 182 times more often than low ones.
claims.quote: only 19% of teams are elite performers, the high-performing cluster shrank from 31% to 22% in a year

value.unit: percent of teams that are elite performers

claims.text: The things SaaS companies refused to build to protect their moats, portability, open schemas, a real API, data you can take out, are precisely the things an agent needs.
claims.quote: The things SaaS companies refused to build, to protect their moats, are precisely the things an agent needs.

claims.text: The mistake is to confuse the brief with a product: SaaS was bought because it is maintained, and the vibe-coded replacement lands every non-functional requirement on an afternoon's work.
claims.quote: The mistake is to confuse the brief with a product.

claims.text: The future is village and town-planner companies that take the finished brief and run it, paid by consumption and by the fact that it keeps working, not by the seat.
claims.quote: Village and town-planner companies. Businesses that take the finished brief, the thing the explorer built, and run it

claims.text: Vibe-coded software is not automatically good, and almost everything vibe coded today runs on frameworks built before generative AI by people who read the code.
claims.quote: almost everything vibe coded today runs on frameworks built before generative AI, by exactly those people, reading exactly that code.

claims.text: The outcome is not fixed: it is still all to play for, and whether the companies on top today come out on top is an open question.
claims.quote: It is still all to play for, and the reason it is worth writing down is that the outcome is not fixed.

claims.text: We will need as many developers as now and probably more, because far more code will be generated and somebody has to read it, harden it and run it.
claims.quote: We are going to need as many developers as we have now, and probably more

claims.text: Much larger, multidisciplinary teams of humans and agents become possible because the communication Fred Brooks said slows projects down can finally be scaled.
claims.quote: I think we can now build much larger, much more multidisciplinary teams of humans and agents, because the communication can finally be scaled
